learning_outcomes.text: Acquire advanced knowledge about new and non-conventional manufacturing processes.
Learn to program machine tools for manufacturing automation.
Evaluate manufacturing time and cost using the appropriate technique.
Know the forming technologies of specific materials for process selection.

syllabus_topics: Forming of specific materials: polymers, glass, rubber, composite materials.
Characteristic elements of an NC machine tool.
Prior concepts and definitions for NC programming.
Manual programming on NC lathe, fixed cycles.
Manual programming on NC milling machine, fixed cycles.
Application of CAD/CAM systems in manufacturing.
Current status and trends of NC.
Application of CAM for generating NC programs.
Simulation of NC programs obtained using CAD/CAM.
Reverse engineering, rapid prototyping, and rapid tooling.

assessment_methods.method: Resolution and submission of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects)

assessment_rules: The course evaluation consists of two parts: theory (50%) and activities (50%), which must be passed independently. The theory part is evaluated through a final exam. The activities part is evaluated through proposed assignments and manufacturing projects. Both parts must be passed individually with a minimum grade of 5 out of 10. Only the activities grade will be saved for subsequent calls within the same academic year. If one part is not passed, the corresponding grade for that call will be the lower of the two.
